title: Excerpt repair and official re-anchoring of the two B8a EXCERPT_MISMATCH case records

method.fetching: Raw curl of the official California Courts opinion-archive PDFs, converted with `pdftotext -layout`. No LLM was used to transcribe any excerpt: every excerpt segment below is a contiguous run of the converted official text and is asserted in code, before any file is written, to be a whitespace-normalized substring of that conversion.
method.joining: Non-contiguous official runs inside one excerpt are joined with ' ... ', the convention already used throughout sources.jsonl.
method.rebuild: Affected tasks were re-assembled by evals/kimi-k3/datasetTools/authorTasks.ts::assembleEvalTask, the same code path that authored B1-B7, so the SOURCE_ENTAILMENT_FAILED guard, the evidence packet, and task_content_sha256 were all recomputed rather than hand-edited. Nothing non-entailed remains.
method.atomicity: sources.jsonl and tasks.jsonl were each rewritten via temp-file-then-rename (os.replace / journal.ts atomicWriteFileSync). Pre-edit backups of sources.jsonl, tasks.jsonl and b3-research-provenance.json were taken in the session scratchpad before any write.
method.idempotence: Re-running provenance/b8b-repair.ts against the repaired dataset reproduced tasks.jsonl byte for byte (sha256 5fabc39abbcb6b99d4d6aadf60f6b4a1d9c4b95495b55e14f85d01dcece90b80).

source_records.what_was_wrong: The stored excerpt came from an aggregator reproduction (animallawconference.org, Casetext-sourced). Word content matched the official opinion but the caption was rendered in aggregator mixed case ('Gregory GEISER ... Peter KUHNS') and the internal quotations used ASCII single quotes; the official opinion capitalizes the caption fully and uses curly double quotation marks. The dataset's verbatim rule authorizes whitespace normalization only, so this was a genuine mismatch.
new_excerpt_segments: IN THE SUPREME COURT OF CALIFORNIA GREGORY GEISER, Plaintiff and Appellant, v. PETER KUHNS et al., Defendants and Appellants. S262032 Second Appellate District, Division Five B279738 Los Angeles County Superior Court BS161018, BS16019, BS161020
August 29, 2022 Justice Liu authored the opinion of the Court, in which Chief Justice Cantil-Sakauye and Justices Corrigan, Kruger, Groban, Jenkins, and Guerrero concurred.
Opinion of the Court by Liu, J.

The Legislature enacted Code of Civil Procedure section 425.16 to combat “a disturbing increase” in Strategic Lawsuits Against Public Participation (SLAPPs): “lawsuits brought primarily to chill the valid exercise of the constitutional rights of freedom of speech and petition for the redress of grievances.”
source_records.legal_content_delta: None. The same legislative-purpose proposition is now quoted in the court's own typography, and the docket/date/authorship block was added so that the record's own text establishes court, docket, filing date, and the fact that the opinion is an opinion of the Court.

source_records.case: Wilson v. Cable News Network, Inc.
source_records.what_was_wrong: The stored vLex-derived excerpt mixed one genuinely verbatim opinion sentence with (a) citation-service caption/parallel-reporter metadata that is not court text and (b) a PARAPHRASED 'Held:' clause that inserted the word 'categorical', which the opinion never uses. This is the more serious of the two findings: a substantive holding proposition rested on paraphrase.
new_excerpt_segments: IN THE SUPREME COURT OF CALIFORNIA STANLEY WILSON, Plaintiff and Appellant, v. CABLE NEWS NETWORK, INC., et al., Defendants and Respondents. S239686 Second Appellate District, Division One B264944 Los Angeles County Superior Court BC559720
July 22, 2019 Justice Kruger authored the opinion of the Court, in which Chief Justice Cantil-Sakauye and Justices Chin, Corrigan, Liu, Cuéllar, and Groban concurred.
Opinion of the Court by Kruger, J.
Plaintiff Stanley Wilson began working for Cable News Network, Inc., in 1996, and wrote and produced stories for the network for more than 17 years.

We hold otherwise. The statute contains no exception for discrimination or retaliation claims, and in some cases the actions a plaintiff alleges in support of his or her claim may qualify as protected speech or petitioning activity under section 425.16. In such cases, the plaintiff’s allegations about the defendant’s invidious motives will not shield the claim from the same preliminary screening for minimal merit that would apply to any other claim arising from protected activity.
source_records.legal_content_delta: Equivalent, and now exact. The paraphrase 'no categorical exception for employment discrimination and retaliation claims' is replaced by the court's own words: 'The statute contains no exception for discrimination or retaliation claims ... the plaintiff's allegations about the defendant's invidious motives will not shield the claim from the same preliminary screening for minimal merit that would apply to any other claim arising from protected activity.' The parallel-reporter citation string, which is not court text, was removed from the excerpt; the official-reports cite 7 Cal.5th 871 remains in the record's locator field and is now separately source-entailed via CIT-INDEX-CAL-5TH-7 (see criterion changes).

new_source_record.role: CITATION METADATA ONLY. Grounds the official-reports page cite '13 Cal.5th 1238' for criterion verification-real-001-c1. No substantive California-law proposition rests on it, and the record's publication_or_precedential_status field says so.
new_source_record.why_needed: The official Geiser slip opinion is a slip opinion; it is filed before the Official Reports assign a volume and page, so it cannot state its own reporter cite. Criterion verification-real-001-c1 asserts that cite.

aggregator_route_tried_and_failed.courtlistener_volume_index: https://www.courtlistener.com/c/cal-5th/13/ indexes only 11 entries for volume 13 Cal.5th, the highest being 13 Cal. 5th 974 -- Geiser at page 1238 is not indexed, so no CIT-INDEX-* record of the B1 kind could be built.

new_source_record.route_used: Full-text search of the official U.S. Government Publishing Office govinfo API (POST https://api.govinfo.gov/search, query "13 Cal. 5th 1238") returned exactly one document, USCOURTS-cand-3_25-cv-03001-1 (Tayts v. Gacutan, N.D.Cal. Jan. 16, 2026), whose text reads: 'In Geiser v. Kuhns, 13 Cal. 5th 1238, 1253-54 (2022), the California Supreme Court clarified ...'. An official federal judicial document is a strictly stronger source for the citation-metadata role than the aggregator the spec already permits for it.
new_source_record.extraction_rule: curl the govinfo.gov permalink; `pdftotext` (no -layout); drop every line consisting solely of digits (the CM/ECF line-number gutter); join remaining lines with single spaces; assert the excerpt is a whitespace-normalized substring of the result.

changes.after: Confirms that a real California Supreme Court decision captioned Geiser v. Kuhns (GREGORY GEISER, Plaintiff and Appellant, v. PETER KUHNS et al., Defendants and Appellants), docket No. S262032, is reported at 13 Cal.5th 1238.
changes.rationale: Legal content preserved. The caption is now stated in the official opinion's own casing, the docket is added because the official record states it, and the reporter-page element -- which previously rested only on the record's locator field -- is now source-entailed by new proposition p4.
